text:
Freddy Gaudreau played his 500th NHL game on November 25, an undrafted center from Bromont, Quebec, who went from the ECHL to Nashville to a long run in Minnesota and now Seattle. He has eight goals in 23 games, already more than his full-season total from last year's numbers.

That pace won't hold. He's scoring on 35% of his shots, against 10% last season, with 8 goals on 4.2 expected. The chances he gets are real, but 23 shots is a thin base for that many goals.

What hasn't changed is his job: penalty killing, and blocked shots (23 so far). Seattle gets only 36.8% of the five-on-five shot attempts with him on the ice, and Evolving-Hockey noted last season that he plays with weaker teammates, which drags those raw numbers down. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking found 20% of his setups come from behind the net, one of the more unusual habits in the league. Watch for that, and for his goal total to flatten as the shooting cools.
